chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from one who informed him, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If the moon is eclipsed and a man wakes up but is too lethargic to perform the prayer, then he must perform ghusl on the following day and make up the prayer. But if he did not wake up and did not know of the eclipse of the moon, then nothing is upon him except making up the prayer without ghusl.

key_terms.فَكَسِلَ: he became sluggish or lazy and failed to act
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةَ: the prayer being discussed, here the eclipse prayer
key_terms.ٱلْقَضَاءُ: the makeup performance of an omitted act of worship
key_terms.ٱلْقَمَرُ: the moon, specifically in the case of a lunar eclipse

ai.seo_question: What must someone do if he misses the salat of a lunar eclipse?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the missed salat of a lunar eclipse. If a person was aware and awake yet neglected it out of laziness, he must perform ghusl and make up the prayer; but if he was unaware and did not wake up, only the makeup prayer is required without ghusl.
